answer: Each agent claims a harbor slot by locking a 70-credit bond, then must cross a tundra segment and reach a summit checkpoint with a receipt signed by the key that booked the slot. The summit auditor checks receipts against the registry and burns the bond of any key whose receipt is missing, late, or signed by another key. Fees escalate: the k-th slot costs 10 + 3(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 3007 and 1000 fake identities pay 1,508,500 in fees plus 70,000 bonds. A rented slot fails because its receipt cannot be re-signed by the renter's key. An honest agent pays one bond and one low fee.
